gloss: halfway; in the middle (of doing something); on the way

definitions.gloss: halfway; in the middle of doing something; partway through
definitions.explanation: Indicates that something happens or is interrupted at an intermediate point during an activity or process, before it is completed.
Indicates that something happens during a journey or while going somewhere, before reaching the destination.

examples.japanese: {映画|えいが}の{途中|とちゅう}で{寝|ね}てしまった。
examples.english: I fell asleep in the middle of the movie.

examples.japanese: {宿題|しゅくだい}を{途中|とちゅう}でやめて{夕食|ゆうしょく}を{食|た}べに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I stopped my homework halfway through and went to have dinner.

examples.japanese: {帰|かえ}り{道|みち}の{途中|とちゅう}でコンビニに{寄|よ}った。
examples.english: On the way home, I stopped by a convenience store.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}に{行|い}く{途中|とちゅう}で{友達|ともだち}に{会|あ}った。
examples.english: I met a friend on the way to the station.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}に{行|い}く{途中|とちゅう}で{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: It started raining on my way to school.

notes:
A very common adverbial expression combining {途中|とちゅう} (middle, midway) + で (locative/instrumental particle). Applies both to actions (partway through) and to journeys (on the way).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {途中|とちゅう}でやめる: to quit partway through
- {途中|とちゅう}で{止|と}まる: to stop in the middle (of something)
- {途中|とちゅう}で{帰|かえ}る: to leave partway through
- {途中|とちゅう}で{気|き}が{変|か}わる: to change one's mind midway
- {帰|かえ}り{道|みち}の{途中|とちゅう}で: on the way home
- {行|い}く{途中|とちゅう}で: on the way (going somewhere)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {途中|とちゅう}{に}: similar meaning, but で is more common when describing an action or event that occurs midway
- {最中|さいちゅう}に: in the middle of — emphasizes the peak of an activity; slightly more formal
- 〜ながら: while doing — describes two simultaneous actions, not interruption

USAGE:
The noun {途中|とちゅう} by itself means "on the way" or "midway." Adding で turns it into an adverbial phrase marking when something else happens.
